title: Enriched vs. Enrichment Media

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Enriched media add nutrients (like blood or serum) to support the growth of fastidious organisms that won't grow on basic media. Enrichment media/broths are used to selectively increase the proportion of a target organism from a mixed sample before plating.
explanation: Despite the similar names, these solve different problems. Enriched media (e.g. blood agar) provide extra nutrition on a solid or liquid medium so a demanding organism can grow at all. Enrichment media/broths are typically liquid, used as a pre-step, and combine nutrients with (often) a selective agent so a target organism outcompetes background flora before it is later streaked onto a plate.

comparison.left: Enriched: supports growth of nutritionally demanding organisms
comparison.right: Enrichment: boosts a target organism's proportion in a mixed sample before isolation

commonMisconceptions: Treating 'enriched' and 'enrichment' as synonyms because they sound alike.
